classification_signals: Abstract: 'This paper carries forth the conceptual framework for biophilic design... New research and insights from the neurosciences, endocrinology and other fields have since helped evolve the scientific basis for biophilic design. This paper begins to articulate this growing body of research and emerging design parameters in architectural terms...'
Introduction: 'The design patterns have been developed from empirical evidence and interdisciplinary analysis of more than 500 peer-reviewed articles and books.'
Results: 'The results of this compilation of research are discussed here for six of the fourteen patterns...'
Extensive citation of existing empirical studies throughout the 'RESULTS' section to support each pattern's claims.
title: BIOPHILIC DESIGN PATTERNS Emerging Nature-Based Parameters for Health and Well-Being in the Built Environment

findings.antecedent: Visual connection with nature (view to living systems and natural processes)
findings.consequent: Reduced stress, more positive emotional functioning, improved concentration, improved recovery rates
findings.source: Pattern 1: Visual Connection With Nature, p. 3
findings.quote: The VISUAL CONNECTION WITH NATURE pattern is derived from data on (1) visual preference and responses to views to nature showing reduced stress, more positive emotional functioning, and improved concentration and recovery rates...

findings.antecedent: People in windowless spaces
findings.consequent: Intuitive addition of nature content, positive response to simulated nature (less strongly than real nature)
findings.source: Pattern 1: Visual Connection With Nature, p. 3
findings.quote: ...adaptation to windowless spaces showing that people intuitively add nature content, and respond positively to simulated nature (although not as strongly as to real nature).

findings.antecedent: Glass window with a nature view (vs. plasma screen with nature video or blank wall)
findings.source: Pattern 1: Visual Connection With Nature, p. 4
findings.quote: ...a glass window with a nature view was, on average, 1.6 times more restorative than each of the other two conditions...

findings.antecedent: Higher levels of biodiversity (in nature exposure)
findings.source: Pattern 1: Visual Connection With Nature, p. 4
findings.quote: According to Fuller, et al. (2007), the psychological benefits of nature increase with higher levels of biodiversity.

findings.antecedent: Viewing scenes of nature (vs. non-nature scenes)
findings.consequent: Stimulation of larger portion of visual cortex, triggering of more pleasure receptors in the brain
findings.source: Pattern 1: Visual Connection With Nature, p. 4
findings.quote: ...viewing scenes of nature stimulates a larger portion of the visual cortex than non-nature scenes and triggers more pleasure receptors in the brain...

findings.antecedent: Repeated viewing of real nature (vs. non-nature)
findings.consequent: Diminishment of viewer's level of interest over time
findings.source: Pattern 1: Visual Connection With Nature, p. 4
findings.quote: ...repeated viewing of real nature, unlike non-nature, does not significantly diminish the viewer's level of interest over time.

findings.antecedent: Exercise within green space (first 5 minutes)
findings.consequent: Positive impact on mood and self-esteem
findings.source: Pattern 1: Visual Connection With Nature, p. 4
findings.quote: Barton and Pretty (2010) argued that positive impact on mood and self-esteem occurs most significantly in the first 5 minutes of exercise within a green space...

findings.antecedent: Viewing nature for 10 minutes prior to experiencing a mental stressor
findings.consequent: Stimulated heart rate variability and parasympathetic activity (regulation of internal organs)
findings.source: Pattern 1: Visual Connection With Nature, p. 4
findings.quote: ...viewing nature for 10 minutes prior to experiencing a mental stressor stimulated heart rate variability and parasympathetic activity...

findings.antecedent: Viewing a forest scene for 20 minutes after a mental stressor
findings.consequent: Cerebral blood flow and brain activity returning to a relaxed state
findings.source: Pattern 1: Visual Connection With Nature, p. 4
findings.quote: ...viewing a forest scene for 20 minutes after a mental stressor returned cerebral blood flow and brain activity to a relaxed state.

findings.antecedent: Non-visual connection with nature (auditory, haptic, olfactory, or gustatory stimuli from nature)
findings.consequent: Reduced systolic blood pressure, reduced stress hormones, improved cognitive performance, improved mental health and tranquility
findings.source: Pattern 2: Non-visual Connection With Nature, p. 4
findings.quote: The NON-VISUAL CONNECTION WITH NATURE pattern is derived from data on reductions in systolic blood pressure and stress hormones... cognitive performance... and perceived improvements in mental health and tranquility...

findings.antecedent: Nature sounds (vs. urban noise)
findings.source: Pattern 2: Non-visual Connection With Nature, p. 5
findings.quote: ...nature sounds, when compared to urban noise, allow for physiological and psychological restoration to occur up to 37% faster after exposure to a psychological stressor.

findings.antecedent: Moderate (70 decibels) ambient noise based on nature sounds
findings.source: Pattern 2: Non-visual Connection With Nature, p. 5
findings.quote: ...moderate (70 decibels) ambient noise had a greater positive impact on creative performance than did exposure to low (50 decibels) or high (>85 decibels) ambient noise.

findings.antecedent: Lavender aromatherapy (in post-anesthesia care unit)
findings.source: Pattern 2: Non-visual Connection With Nature, p. 5
findings.quote: ...lavender aromatherapy in the post-anesthesia care unit reduces opioid requirements of morbidly obese patients undergoing laparoscopic adjustable gastric banding.

findings.antecedent: Phytoncides (essential oils from trees)
findings.source: Pattern 2: Non-visual Connection With Nature, p. 5
findings.quote: ...phytoncides (essential oils from trees) had a positive effect on human immune function both in vitro and in vivo.

findings.antecedent: Visual and non-visual stimuli from nature experienced simultaneously
findings.consequent: Excitation of larger portion of the brain, more impactful psychophysiological response
findings.source: Pattern 2: Non-visual Connection With Nature, p. 5
findings.quote: ...experiencing visual and non-visual stimuli simultaneously changes where in the brain the non-visual senses are interpreted; whereby, if both stimuli are connections with nature, a larger portion of the brain becomes excited and the combined psychophysiological response is more impactful than two responses in isolation.

findings.antecedent: Access to thermal and airflow variability (ambient qualities like air temperature, relative humidity, airflow, radiant temperature that vary)
findings.consequent: Feelings of comfort similar to those experienced in nature
findings.source: Pattern 4: Access To Thermal And Airflow Variability, p. 5
findings.quote: ACCESS TO THERMAL AND AIRFLOW VARIABILITY can be characterized as ambient qualities – air temperature, relative humidity, airflow across the skin, and the radiant temperature of surrounding surfaces – that in combination prompt feelings of comfort similar to those experienced in nature.

findings.antecedent: Moderate levels of sensory variability (light, sound, temperatures)
findings.source: Pattern 4: Access To Thermal And Airflow Variability, p. 5
findings.quote: ...people like moderate levels of sensory variability in the environment, including variation in light, sound and temperatures...

findings.antecedent: Environment devoid of sensory stimulation and variability
findings.source: Pattern 4: Access To Thermal And Airflow Variability, p. 5
findings.quote: ...an environment devoid of sensory stimulation and variability can lead to boredom and passivity...

findings.antecedent: Pleasant thermal sensations (alliesthesia) when one's initial body state is warm or cold (not neutral)
findings.source: Pattern 4: Access To Thermal And Airflow Variability, p. 6
findings.quote: Early studies in alliesthesia indicate that pleasant thermal sensations are better perceived when one's initial body state is warm or cold, not neutral...

findings.antecedent: Temporary over-cooling of a small portion of the body when hot, or over-heating when cold (without impacting core temperature)
findings.source: Pattern 4: Access To Thermal And Airflow Variability, p. 6
findings.quote: ...a temporary over-cooling of a small portion of the body when hot, or over-heating when cold, even without really impacting the body's overall core temperature, is perceived as highly comfortable.

findings.antecedent: Light breezes or other natural movements ('soft fascination')
findings.source: Pattern 4: Access To Thermal And Airflow Variability, p. 6
findings.quote: ...elements of 'soft fascination' such as light breezes or other natural movements can improve concentration...

findings.antecedent: Changes in ventilation velocity
findings.source: Pattern 4: Access To Thermal And Airflow Variability, p. 6
findings.quote: ...changes in ventilation velocity can have a positive impact on comfort, with no negative impact on cognitive function, while also offering the possibility of a slight increase in the ability to access short term memory...

findings.antecedent: Changes in ventilation velocity
findings.source: Pattern 4: Access To Thermal And Airflow Variability, p. 6
findings.quote: ...changes in ventilation velocity can have a positive impact on comfort, with no negative impact on cognitive function, while also offering the possibility of a slight increase in the ability to access short term memory...

findings.antecedent: Changes in ventilation velocity
findings.source: Pattern 4: Access To Thermal And Airflow Variability, p. 6
findings.quote: ...changes in ventilation velocity can have a positive impact on comfort, with no negative impact on cognitive function, while also offering the possibility of a slight increase in the ability to access short term memory...

findings.antecedent: Gradient of thermal conditions within a classroom
findings.source: Pattern 4: Access To Thermal And Airflow Variability, p. 6
findings.quote: ...a gradient of thermal conditions within a classroom can lead to better student performance.

findings.antecedent: Features allowing users to easily adapt and modify their perceived thermal conditions
findings.consequent: Range of acceptable temperatures (by two degrees Celsius above and below conventional parameters)
findings.source: Pattern 4: Access To Thermal And Airflow Variability, p. 6
findings.quote: Provide features that allow users to easily adapt and modify their perceived thermal conditions of their environment will increase the range of acceptable temperatures by two degrees Celsius above and below the conventional parameters for thermal comfort...

findings.antecedent: Presence of water elements (visual, auditory, tactile)
findings.consequent: Enhanced experience of space, positive emotional responses, reduced stress, increased tranquility, lower heart rate, lower blood pressure, recovered skin conductance, improved concentration, improved memory restoration, enhanced perception and psychophysiological responsiveness (when multiple senses stimulated)
findings.source: Pattern 5: Presence Of Water, p. 6
findings.quote: The PRESENCE OF WATER pattern has evolved from research on visual preference for and positive emotional responses to environments containing water elements... reduced stress, increased feelings of tranquility, lower heart rate and blood pressure, and recovered skin conductance... improved concentration and memory restoration... and enhanced perception and psychological and physiological responsiveness when multiple senses are stimulated simultaneously...

findings.antecedent: Natural scenes without a water body, and urban scenes with water elements
findings.source: Pattern 5: Presence Of Water, p. 6
findings.quote: ...natural scenes without a water body, and urban scenes with water elements, exhibit near equal health benefits to participants...

findings.antecedent: Unnatural or urban scenes (generally)
findings.source: Pattern 5: Presence Of Water, p. 6
findings.quote: ...unnatural or urban scenes generally engender less pleasurable or restorative effects.

findings.antecedent: Auditory access and perceived/potential tactile access to water
findings.source: Pattern 5: Presence Of Water, p. 6
findings.quote: ...auditory access and perceived or potential tactile access to water reduced stress in participants...

findings.antecedent: Activities conducted in green spaces with the presence of water (vs. without water)
findings.source: Pattern 5: Presence Of Water, p. 6
findings.quote: ...activities conducted in green spaces with the presence of water generated greater improvements in both self-esteem and mood than green environments without the presence of water.

findings.antecedent: Water perceived as clean
findings.source: Pattern 5: Presence Of Water, p. 6
findings.quote: Water should be perceived as clean (Orians and Heerwagen, 1992).

findings.antecedent: Multi-sensory water experience
findings.source: Pattern 5: Presence Of Water, p. 7
findings.quote: Prioritize a multi-sensory water experience (Alvarsson et al., 2010; Hunter et al., 2010; Pheasant et al., 2010).

findings.antecedent: Naturally fluctuating water movement (vs. predictable movement or stagnancy)
findings.source: Pattern 5: Presence Of Water, p. 7
findings.quote: Prioritize naturally fluctuating water movement over predictable movement or stagnancy (Alversson et al., 2010; Biederman & Vessel, 2006).

findings.antecedent: Complexity and Order (rich sensory information configured with a coherent spatial hierarchy)
findings.source: Pattern 10: Complexity And Order, p. 7
findings.quote: COMPLEXITY AND ORDER is characterized by the presence of rich sensory information that is configured with a coherent spatial hierarchy, similar to the occurrence of design in nature.

findings.antecedent: Fractal geometries in nature, art, and architecture (dimensional ratio D=1.3-1.8)
findings.source: Pattern 10: Complexity And Order, p. 7
findings.quote: ...the perceptual and physiological stress responses to the complexity of fractals in nature, art and architecture...

findings.antecedent: Nested fractal designs (third iteration of base design, scaling factor of 3)
findings.source: Pattern 10: Complexity And Order, p. 7
findings.quote: Nested fractal designs expressed as a third iteration of the base design (i.e., with scaling factor of 3) are more likely to achieve a level of complexity that conveys reduces stress...

findings.antecedent: High-dimensional fractal artwork and overly complex environments
findings.source: Pattern 10: Complexity And Order, p. 7
findings.quote: ...high-dimensional fractal artwork and overly complex environments can result in psychological stress and even nausea.

findings.antecedent: Interaction of multiple wallpaper patterns, complex carpet patterns, moiré patterns in seating fabrics
findings.consequent: Surfaces appearing to move, extreme visual perception problems (nausea, headaches, dizziness)
findings.source: Pattern 10: Complexity And Order, p. 7
findings.quote: ...the interaction of multiple wall paper patterns, complex patterns in carpets and moiré patterns in seating fabrics caused surfaces to appear to move as occupants walked through the space and therefore caused extreme visual perception problems...

findings.antecedent: Prospect (unimpeded view over a distance for surveillance and planning)
findings.consequent: Reduced stress, reduced boredom, irritation, fatigue, reduced perceived vulnerability, improved comfort
findings.source: Pattern 11: Prospect, p. 8
findings.quote: Health benefits are suggested to include reduced stress... reduced boredom, irritation, fatigue... and perceived vulnerability... as well as improved comfort...

findings.antecedent: Prospect condition including savannah-like ecosystem, water body, and evidence of human activity/habitation
findings.source: Pattern 11: Prospect, p. 8
findings.quote: ...preference for a prospect condition is strongest when it includes a savannah-like ecosystem with a water body and evidence of human activity or habitation.

findings.antecedent: Good prospect
findings.consequent: Individual's fear and stress responses (especially when alone or in new/unfamiliar environments)
findings.source: Pattern 11: Prospect, p. 8
findings.quote: ...good prospect reduces an individual's fear and stress responses, particularly when alone or in new or unfamiliar environments...

findings.antecedent: Distant prospect (>100 feet, >30 meters) (vs. shorter focal lengths <20 feet, 6 meters)
findings.source: Pattern 11: Prospect, p. 8
findings.quote: ...distant prospect (>100 feet, >30 meters) is preferred over shorter focal lengths (<20 feet, 6 meter) because it provides a greater sense of awareness and comfort.

findings.antecedent: Interior spaces with ability to see from one space to another, clear distinctions, and opportunity to see through multiple spaces
findings.source: Pattern 11: Prospect, p. 8
findings.quote: For interior spaces or dense urban spaces, prospect is the ability to see from one space to another, and is strengthened when there are clear distinctions and the opportunity to see through multiple spaces...

findings.antecedent: Mystery (partially obscured views or other sensory stimuli that fascinate and entice)
findings.consequent: Individual travels deeper into the environment, strong pleasure response (similar to anticipation)
findings.source: Pattern 13: Mystery, p. 8
findings.quote: MYSTERY is a spatial condition characterized by the promise of more information manifested by the presence of partially obscured views or other sensory stimuli that fascinate and entice the individual to travel deeper into the environment...

findings.antecedent: Quality mystery condition (vs. fear-inducing)
findings.source: Pattern 13: Mystery, p. 8
findings.quote: A quality mystery condition does not engender a fear response; the conditions that differentiate between fear and pleasure center around the visual depth of field.

findings.antecedent: Obscured view with limited visual access
findings.source: Pattern 13: Mystery, p. 9
findings.quote: ...obscured view with limited visual access can lead to unpleasant surprises...

findings.antecedent: Greater visual access with medium (≥20 ft) to high (≥100 ft) depth of field
findings.source: Pattern 13: Mystery, p. 9
findings.quote: ...a greater visual access, with a medium (≥20 ft) to high (≥100 ft) depth of field is preferred.

findings.antecedent: Good mystery condition (obscures boundaries, portion of forward plane of subject object/room/building/outdoor space/information source)
findings.consequent: Enticement to explore space, see more of partially obscured subject
findings.source: Pattern 13: Mystery, p. 9
findings.quote: ...a good mystery condition obscures the boundaries and a portion of the forward plane of the subject object, room, building, outdoor space, or other information source, thereby enticing the user to explore the space, to see more of the partially obscured subject.

limitations: Need for understanding where numeric metrics are necessary and where qualitative attributes are more appropriate for biophilic design.
Lack of research on the frequency and duration of exposure to biophilic patterns required for positive health impacts.
Lack of research on the persistence of positive health responses after a biophilic intervention.
Uncertainty regarding whether biophilic experiences, particularly Mystery, attenuate with familiarity.
Lack of understanding on the quantity or percentage of objects in a view shed required for an adequate positive health response (e.g., specific fractal ratios).
Some aspects of biophilia are inherently difficult to quantify due to the field's infancy.
Challenges in tracking and measuring efficacy due to high number of variables, shifting baselines, unpredictability of environments, and invasive data collection techniques.
External factors like genetics, diet, exercise, and socio-economic status impact baselines for stress measurement.
The definition of 'nature' is in perpetual flux across cultures and generations, making it difficult to establish a baseline for evidence.
Need for clear definitions, metrics, and guidelines for planning, design implementation, monitoring, and validation of efficacy.
minimum_safe_summary: This paper synthesizes existing research to articulate a conceptual framework for biophilic design, proposing 14 patterns (with 6 discussed in detail) that connect human-nature relationships to health and well-being in the built environment. Key findings indicate that visual and non-visual connections to nature, thermal and airflow variability, presence of water, complexity and order (especially fractal patterns), prospect, and mystery can reduce stress, improve cognitive performance, enhance mood, and increase comfort. The paper highlights limitations including the need for quantitative metrics, understanding of dose-response, persistence of effects, and the impact of habituation, as well as challenges in measuring efficacy due to numerous confounding variables and the evolving definition of 'nature'.

paper_metadata.crossref_abstract: This paper carries forth the conceptual framework for biophilic design that was first laid out by Cramer and Browning in Biophilic Design (2008), which established three categories meant to help define biophilic buildings – Nature in the Space, Natural Analogues and Nature of the Space – and a preliminary list of “biophilic conditions”. New research and insights from the neurosciences, endocrinology and other fields have since helped evolve the scientific basis for biophilic design. This paper begins to articulate this growing body of research and emerging design parameters in architectural terms, so that we may draw connections between fields of study, highlight potential avenues for future research, evolve our understanding of biophilic design patterns, and capture the positive psychophysiological and cognitive benefits afforded by biophilia in our design interventions.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: Humans have an innate tendency to connect with nature and other living systems, which is essential for their health and well-being.
Exposure to natural environments can restore directed attention by engaging involuntary attention, leading to improved concentration and cognitive functioning.
Exposure to natural environments can reduce physiological and psychological stress, leading to more positive emotional functioning and improved recovery rates.
